title: Cambodia faces a difficult path to elections
text: Cambodia's parliamentary elections are two years away. That is a short period, given that the position of the current political regime of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) remains uncertain. Although the party performed well in the municipal elections in 2015, there is no confidence that it can win and retain power in the parliamentary elections. The CPP faces many problems. Chief among them are corruption in the party, nepotism and detachment from the people, who, according to analysts, have long been tired of seeing the same governing figures at the top of Cambodia's political hierarchy. There is also a perception that the party leadership does not plan to renew its policy or introduce new leaders, even if it recognises its problems. In January 2015, at an emergency session of the CPP, it was noted that “the corruption, nepotism, abuse of powers, violation of the laws spread among the Party’s members had undermined the confidence of the people and raised doubts about its right to rule the country.” At the session, the introduction of reforms within the party and society was described as a matter of life and death for the CPP's future. However, almost two years have passed since the session, and the party has not begun to address its serious problems. Its leadership includes no new, young and appealing leaders, although at the provincial level there are competent and respected provincial governors, CPP members who could change the image of the ruling party if they joined its leadership.

title: Bitter, nasty and maybe the last: Sanders and Clinton's debate turns ugly
text: If Bernie Sanders stuns the pollsters and defies expectations in the New York primary on Tuesday, April 19, his backers and staff will be shouting about his ninth debate with rival Hillary Clinton on the night of April 14. They will claim that Sanders' relentlessly aggressive strategy in the latest CNN debate, with its nonstop barrage of attacks on Clinton, was the defining moment in a long campaign for a nomination that is still up for grabs. And they will have some basis for saying so. But what if Sanders' assault does not bring victory next week? Then this Brooklyn showdown may mark the beginning of the end for Sanders' remarkable long-shot run. It may also be the last debate in either party in this historically long and brutal contest for the major party nominations. This time, the gloves were off. Both Sanders and Clinton showed flashes of animosity bordering on contempt. When Sanders suggested Clinton's 250-delegate lead was rooted in the deeply conservative Deep South, where he said she had "cleaned our clock," Clinton angrily fired back a list of states she had won outside that region. When Clinton said she had "called out" the big banks after the 2008 mortgage meltdown, Sanders could not hold back the sarcasm: "They must have been very upset by this," he said, drawing howls of glee from his large contingent in the audience. The crowd was wild from start to finish. Each candidate's supporters cheered loudly, not just at the end of answers but often at every sentence or phrase. At times the rowdy battle between the rival camps felt like dueling grandstands at a high school basketball game. And they had more than enough provocation!

title: "No way to turn back this tide": Biden fires warning shot at Trump on climate
text: Can Donald Trump really tear up the green agenda? Not much of it, U.S. Vice President Joe Biden said on Friday, because so many environmental policies have now firmly taken root. Trump, who takes over as president on Jan. 20, has said he does not believe in global warming, and he will name a climate change skeptic, Oklahoma Attorney General Scott Pruitt, to run the Environmental Protection Agency. And he is not stopping there. The Republican is expected to nominate another climate change skeptic, U.S. Representative Cathy McMorris Rodgers of Washington state, to head the Interior Department, sources briefed on the matter said on Friday. Democratic President Barack Obama has made the fight against global warming a priority, and Biden said businesses now realized his policies made economic sense. “There is a constituency that crosses party lines. Regardless of whether the next administration is as aggressive as we have been - and I’m not suggesting they intend to - there is no way to turn back this tide that has begun to roll,” the vice president told a Canadian environmental summit. The Obama administration has raised vehicle fuel standards, poured money into renewable energy, pushed to curb methane gas emissions and adopted a Clean Power Plan requiring states to cut carbon output. And the market is on its side! Biden said that in some parts of the United States it was now cheaper to use solar or wind power than to rely on power stations fueled by coal or gas. Company executives were starting to price in carbon emissions reduction, while motorists enjoyed refueling their vehicles less often, he said. His blunt verdict? “Reality has a way of intruding,” he said.

title: Gold rush or hot air? U.S. gas giants scramble for a slice of China's LNG boom
text: The race is on! U.S. gas exporters and traders are hungry for a bigger piece of the lucrative, booming business of exporting gas to China, the world's third-largest buyer, when they join Commerce Secretary Wilbur Ross on his trip to China next month. But could it all be hot air? If U.S. suppliers can't compete with the bargain prices locked in on long-term deals with rivals Australia, Qatar and Malaysia, it just might be. According to a list of the participants, 10 of the 29 companies traveling with Ross and U.S. President Donald Trump are involved in energy and gas. Among them are Cheniere Energy Inc, which operates the only U.S. LNG export terminal, and Freepoint Commodities, founded and run by David Messer, who led power utility Sempra's vaunted commodities division. Their presence shows just how badly the U.S. wants to sell more of its excess gas abroad, as the U.S. shale revolution threatens to shake up the global LNG market. And China's appetite is enormous. It has soared as Beijing embarks on an audacious bid to heat millions of homes across the north with gas for the first time this winter and switch tens of thousands of industrial boilers to the cleaner fuel as part of its push to clear the skies. Without enough domestic output to meet growing demand, imports have surged this year, a huge opportunity for major exporting nations such as the United States. "We're on the mission to talk to Chinese companies to get something signed up," said Frederick Jones, founder and chief executive of Delfin Midstream LLC, which is building floating LNG vessels that would sit 50 miles off the coast of Louisiana. He is heading to Beijing with his chief financial officer Matthew Weil on the trip, which is scheduled to begin on Nov. 8.

title: Daily Show segment examines Republican bathroom bills
text: On Wednesday night, Daily Show correspondent Jessica Williams addressed the bathroom bills that GOP lawmakers have made a focus of their efforts to harass and discriminate against the LGBT community. As the transgender community has gained visibility, Republican legislators have put more energy into proposing anti-transgender bills that regulate which bathrooms transgender people can and cannot use. To understand why, Williams spoke to several trans people and to one of their leading opponents, Chaplain and state Rep. Gordon Klingenschmitt (R-CO). Williams questioned the lawmaker, who opposes transgender rights, about his belief that transgender people are merely confused, and he did not hold up under the questioning. Explaining his religious beliefs, Klingenschmitt told Williams why transgender people were a threat to the rest of the country: They not only want to be confused about their own identity, but they want the rest of us to be confused with them. Now they want the government to join them on that pretense? They're making us into liars. When Williams asked trans people what they wanted, however, they said they wanted respect. They said they were not trying to confuse or trick anyone about their identity and that their gender identity was not a choice, a point research can confirm. Klingenschmitt wanted to discuss religion further, but insisted on changing first. He said: I would be comfortable talking about religious freedom, but I have to change into my alter ego. Williams waited for him to transition so he would feel more comfortable during the interview, and Klingenschmitt did not appear to notice the irony of the situation. When Williams asked Klingenschmitt why he was so committed to passing anti-transgender legislation, he replied: I mean, that is perversion.

title: Could Yelp fix patient care? The surprising power of online reviews!
text: Hospitals and many insurance carriers care deeply about patient satisfaction. It matters especially to hospitals, because insurance payments can hinge on how patients rate the care they receive, as well as on the health of the patient, which hospitals usually report. Yet many in the health care profession can't stand this. They argue that patient satisfaction scores aren't necessarily aligned with outcomes. Worse, they say, trying to improve satisfaction is a waste of time. But what if patient satisfaction is already being rewarded, and all the effort to highlight it isn't helping nearly as much as we think? Almost every study on patient satisfaction relies on the Hospital Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (H. C. A. H. P. S.) survey. Studies show it is correlated with clinical measures of quality, although some other studies dispute this. And collecting such information is costly! There may be other sources for quality assessments that don't require a cent of investment from the health care system. In 2012, researchers in the Journal of General Internal Medicine dug into online reviews from RateMDs. com and Yelp. The finding? A majority of reviews were positive. But patients reported on aspects of care that went beyond the encounter. They cared about staff, access to the hospital and convenience. And they cared enormously about the bedside manner of the doctors they met. Dr. Naomi Bardach, associate professor of pediatrics and health policy at U. C. S. F. Benioff Children's Hospital San Francisco, and her colleagues turned to Yelp to see how consumer ratings stacked up against the hospital consumer assessment survey. Of the almost 3, 800 hospitals with survey and other data, about 25 percent also had ratings on Yelp.

title: Pope Francis comes face to face with Myanmar's army chief amid Rohingya horror
text: A high-stakes encounter! Pope Francis held talks on Monday with Myanmar's military chief at the start of a delicate visit to a majority-Buddhist country that the United States has accused of ethnic cleansing against its Muslim Rohingya people. The leader of the Roman Catholic church will also visit Bangladesh, where more than 620,000 Rohingya have fled to escape what Amnesty International has called "crimes against humanity". Myanmar's army has denied the accusations of murder, rape, torture and forced displacement made against it. The pope's very first meeting in Yangon was with military commander Senior General Min Aung Hlaing in St. Mary's Cathedral in the heart of the Southeast Asian nation's largest city. They discussed "the great responsibility of authorities of the country in this time of transition", Vatican spokesman Greg Burke said after the 15 minutes of talks, which were followed by an exchange of gifts. Francis presented the general with a commemorative medal of his visit, and Min Aung Hlaing gave the pope a harp in the shape of a boat and an ornate rice bowl, Burke said. And the army chief's message? He told the pope that "there's no religious discrimination in Myanmar" and "there's the freedom of religion", according to a statement on the Facebook page of Min Aung Hlaing. "Every soldier's goal is to build a stable and peaceful country," the army chief was paraphrased as saying in the statement. No discrimination? Members of ethnic minority groups in traditional dress welcomed Francis at Yangon airport, and children presented him with flowers as he stepped off his plane. He waved through an open window at dozens of children waving Vatican and Myanmar flags and wearing T-shirts with the motto of the trip, "love and peace", as he set off in a car.

title: UNESCO committee passes resolution on Jerusalem holy site despite Israeli objections
text: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) has approved a motion that endorses the right of the Palestinians to the al-Aqsa Mosque compound and criticizes Israeli provocations around the holy site. UNESCO's 21-member World Heritage Committee adopted the resolution in a secret ballot on Wednesday at the agency's headquarters in Paris. Ten countries voted in favor, two against and eight abstained, while one was absent. The resolution expresses UNESCO's deep concerns over Israeli construction works and archaeological excavations in the Old City of Jerusalem al-Quds. Saeb Erekat, the secretary general of the Palestine Liberation Organization, welcomed the passage of the motion and accused the Israeli government of conducting a campaign of distorting facts in order to legitimize its occupation of East Jerusalem al-Quds. “Through an orchestrated campaign, Israel has been using archaeological claims and distortion of facts as a way to legitimize the annexation of occupied East Jerusalem,” Erekat said. He also noted that the UNESCO resolution calls for “respecting the status quo of its religious sites, including the al-Aqsa Mosque compound that continues to be threatened by the systematic incitement and provocative actions of the Israeli government and extremist Jewish groups.” Earlier this month, UNESCO's 58-member Executive Board approved a similar resolution, which drew a strong reaction from Israel, and Israel suspended its ties with the agency. Wednesday's vote drew further objection from Israel, and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that Israel's ambassador to UNESCO, Carmel Shama-Hacohen, had been recalled for consultations. “We will decide what the next steps will be,” Netanyahu said in a statement. Elias Sanbar, Palestine's UNESCO envoy, responded to critics of the resolution and said that Israelis were “politicizing religion and this is very dangerous.”

title: Photos of Sylville Smith published after Milwaukee police shooting and unrest
text: Syville Smith had a gun that had been stolen during a burglary in a suburb of Milwaukee, along with 500 rounds of ammunition. A police officer told Smith to put the stolen gun down as he was fleeing from officers after a traffic stop. He refused. He was killed, and people are now burning down the city of Milwaukee in his honor. A standoff between police and a crowd turned violent Saturday night in the hours after a Milwaukee police officer shot and killed an armed suspect during a foot chase on the city's north side. City police officials said two officers stopped two suspects in a car at about 3:30 p.m. The suspects then ran. During the pursuit, a six-year veteran of the department shot and killed a 23-year-old Milwaukee resident who was carrying a semiautomatic handgun, police said. The officer was not hurt. During a midnight news conference, Mayor Barrett said the officer pursuing the 23-year-old man ordered him to drop his gun. The man did not, and the officer fired several times, the mayor said. The man was hit twice, once in the chest and once in the arm. Barrett said police determined there were 23 rounds in the man's gun. He said the officer was wearing a body camera and that, to his understanding, the camera was operating during the incident. Several pictures were also found on Smith's Facebook account. Smith had a criminal record. Court records show that in February of 2015, Smith was charged with one felony count of first degree recklessly endangering safety and one misdemeanor count of possession of THC. Prosecutors dismissed the charges in November. In August of 2015, Smith was charged with felony intimidation of a witness/person charged/felony.

title: Man killed by Milwaukee police had stolen gun and prior charges
text: Syville Smith, 23, who was shot and killed by a Milwaukee police officer during a foot chase on the city's north side, had a gun stolen during a burglary in a Milwaukee suburb, along with 500 rounds of ammunition. He refused an officer's order to put the gun down as he fled after a traffic stop. A standoff between police and a crowd turned violent Saturday night in the hours after the shooting, and people are burning down the city in his honor. Police officials said two officers stopped two suspects in a car at about 3:30 p.m. The suspects fled on foot. A six-year veteran of the department shot the man, who was carrying a semiautomatic handgun. The officer was not hurt. Mayor Barrett told a midnight news conference that the man did not drop his gun when ordered and the officer fired several times. The man was hit twice, in the chest and the arm. Police found 23 rounds in his gun. Barrett said the officer wore a body camera that he understood was operating during the incident. Pictures were found on Smith's Facebook account. Court records show Smith was charged in February of 2015 with one felony count of first degree recklessly endangering safety and one misdemeanor count of possession of THC. Prosecutors dismissed the charges in November. In August of 2015, Smith was charged with felony intimidation of a witness/person charged/felony.

title: Rick Santorum advises President Trump to stop tweeting; Trump continues to post on Twitter
text: In a recent interview with CNN, former senator and Republican presidential candidate Rick Santorum suggested that President Trump's time in office so far would have been more successful, and that he could still become a better leader, if he made one change: stop tweeting. During the Sunday morning edition of State of the Union with Dana Bash, Santorum stated his view directly. "If you tweet every day and complain about the media and complain about how you are being treated, you're going to be sidetracked and you're not going to get your deals done. That's the message," Santorum said, looking straight into the camera and using terms the president could relate to in order to convey his advice. Donald Trump had just concluded his first overseas trip as President of the United States, a nine-day journey to the Middle East, during which he used social media much less and stayed focused on the trip. Shortly after his return to the White House, however, the President took to Twitter to express displeasure on a number of topics, mainly opinions that differ from his own, using what has become his latest catchphrase, the Fake News. "British Prime Minister May was very angry that the info the U.K. gave to U.S. about Manchester was leaked. Gave me full details!" Trump wrote on May 28, 2017. In another post, he wrote: "Does anyone notice how the Montana Congressional race was such a big deal to Dems & Fake News until the Republican won?"

title: House committee votes to keep Confederate flag at The Citadel; Democrats plan to continue effort
text: Democrats are again seeking to remove a historical symbol at The Citadel. U.S. Rep. Jim Clyburn is determined to pursue the issue until the flag is removed. There are more pressing issues to address. Early on Thursday morning, the U.S. House Armed Services Committee voted to keep the Confederate flag flying at The Citadel. The rejection of a Democratic effort to force the military institution to take down the flag atop Summerall Chapel may set up an extended dispute over the issue, which is being led by U.S. Rep. Jim Clyburn, D-S.C. U.S. Rep. Adam Smith, a Washington State Democrat and ranking member of the committee, offered an amendment to the fiscal 2017 National Defense Authorization Act to bar Reserve Officers Training Corps funds to any military university that displays the Confederate flag. The only university in that category is The Citadel. The Board of Visitors voted to remove the flag last summer, after it was revealed that the shooting of nine black parishioners at Mother Emanuel AME Church was racially motivated. That incident also led to the removal of the Confederate flag from the Statehouse grounds. The Board of Visitors says, however, that it cannot take the flag down unless the S.C. state legislature changes the so-called Heritage Act, which currently prevents its removal. Smith acknowledged that his amendment was intended to force state lawmakers to act.

title: Atheist group sues Texas governor over removal of Capitol display
text: The Freedom From Religion Foundation, an atheist group, created a display parodying a nativity scene and then sued the Texas governor when he removed it. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott is being sued by the group over his decision to remove its nativity-scene parody from the state Capitol in December. The Freedom From Religion Foundation announced a federal lawsuit against Abbott in the Western District of Texas, Austin division, on Thursday. The organization alleges that the governor violated free speech, equal protection and due process rights when he ordered the removal of an exhibit commemorating the birth of the Bill of Rights. The image, approved by the Texas State Preservation Board, showed the Statue of Liberty, the Founding Fathers and the Bill of Rights in a manger. It was placed in the state Capitol on Dec. 18, 2015, and remained there for three days before Abbott acted. "Mocking the Capitol nativity scene is offensive. I demand the removal of the satirical nativity scene from Capitol," Abbott tweeted on Dec. 22, 2015. The governor also wrote a letter to the State Preservation Board: "This juvenile parody violates the Preservation Board's regulations and should be removed immediately. The biblical scene of the newly born Jesus Christ lying in a manger in Bethlehem lies at the very heart of the Christian faith. Subjecting an image held sacred by millions of Texans to the Foundation's tasteless sarcasm does nothing to promote morals and the general welfare," Abbott said. The group frequently objects to religious displays, and this is the latest case in which it has challenged one.

title: Hannity and Cruz exchange sharp words over delegate process
text: GOP presidential candidate Texas Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX) and talk radio and Fox News Channel host Sean Hannity had a tense exchange over the delegate process on Hannity's radio show on Tuesday. And everybody's asking me this question. So, I want I'm giving you an opportunity to explain it." Cruz responded, "Sean, the only people asking this question, are the hardcore Donald Trump supporters." Hannity interrupted again to ask, "Senator, why do you this?"

title: Second bomb-making stash found near Paris! Suspects claimed a bank heist — police see terror
text: Another chilling discovery! French police unearthed a second stash of explosive materials near Paris on Thursday after a similar find in a nearby suburb on Wednesday, a justice official said as three suspects were grilled by anti-terrorism investigators. Thursday's swoop hit a garage rented by one of the three detained after Wednesday's raid on an apartment in Villejuif, on the southern edge of the French capital, the source said. Materials used to produce TATP, an explosive often used by suicide bombers, were found at the flat after a plumber phoned police to report suspicious activity there, Interior Minister Gerard Collomb said. A plumber! Two people in their 30s and 40s were arrested immediately after Wednesday's raid, said Collomb, who added that the suspects were being questioned on suspicion of terrorist activity despite talking of a bank heist. A third man was arrested overnight, a source said. "Those under investigation spoke of wanting to blow up a bank with the TATP but the way we see it is they have links with terrorism, and this is the channel of investigation," Collomb told public radio station franceinfo. That line of inquiry was prompted by information found in telephone communications after the raid, he added. The minister spoke before later developments in which police found explosive materials at a garage in Thiais, southeast of Paris. The toll of terror in France is staggering: more than 230 people have been killed by Islamist-inspired attackers in the past three years in France, which along with the United States and other countries is bombing Islamic State bases in Iraq and Syria. And TATP, an unstable explosive, has been used by militants in several attacks in western Europe in recent years, including Manchester in May, Brussels in 2016 and Paris in 2015.

title: From unknown to icon overnight: the 11-year-old who became a hero to Latinas!
text: What a transformation! Just a few months ago, Sarai Gonzalez's proudest distinction was being a funny older sister. She hammed it up during dance parties in her family room in Green Brook, N. J. She wore studded pink and baked a mean cupcake. Now? Sarai, 11, is in a Get Out the Vote ad. Miranda is praising her on Twitter. She recently attended an event for Hispanic Heritage at the White House, where she hugged the president and was mobbed for selfies, wearing a blue satin gown. “It was like a flash,” Sarai said. In record time, she went from unknown little girl to Latina icon, all thanks to a viral music video: Sarai is the nerdy, round and confident tween who stands up to bullies on the streets of Brooklyn in the video for “Soy Yo” or “That’s Me,” by the Colombian group Bomba Estéreo. If you're Latina, chances are you've already seen her. The video, released by the band last month, racked up a million views in its first days. (It now has more than six million!) It was featured everywhere, from NBC News to Fusion. It spawned a hashtag, schoolchildren's art, and animated GIFs, which in turn became memes. “Soy Yo” seemed to arrive at exactly the right moment — a defiant, and adorable, rebuke to the rhetoric of the Trump campaign, and haters in general. “Don’t worry if they don’t accept you,” goes the song's chorus, in Spanish. “If they criticize you, just say, ‘That’s me.’ ” The video struck a powerful chord with Latinas. Rarely in American life, especially in an era of ugly debates over immigrants, had popular culture created a young, brown character so heroic, free of victimhood, full of dignity. Sarai made Latinas visible. Real Latinas. And they answered, in a chorus of “yes, that’s me.”

title: Showdown looms: Trump advisers meet to decide fate of the Paris climate deal
text: Decision time! Advisers to President Donald Trump will meet on Tuesday to discuss whether to recommend that he pull the United States out of the Paris climate accord, a White House official said on Monday. The accord, agreed on by nearly 200 countries in Paris in 2015, aims to limit planetary warming in part by slashing carbon dioxide and other emissions from the burning of fossil fuels. Under the pact, the United States committed to cutting its emissions by 26 to 28 percent from 2005 levels by 2025. Trump has said the United States should “cancel” the deal, but he has gone mostly quiet on the issue since he was elected last November. Environmental groups want Washington to stay in the Paris agreement, even if the new administration weakens U.S. pledges. A White House official said Trump's aides would “discuss the options, with the goal of providing a recommendation to the president about the path forward.” The clock is ticking: the meeting comes before a summit of the Group of Seven wealthy nations in late May, the deadline for the White House to take a position. White House officials, led by the National Economic Council, have recently been asking publicly traded energy companies for advice on whether to stay in. And the answer from some energy companies may surprise you. Peabody Energy has consulted with White House officials, and Cloud Peak Energy Inc confirmed it had told White House advisers it was in its interests for the United States to remain in the agreement to ensure a global role for high-efficiency coal plants. On Monday, liquified natural gas exporter Cheniere Energy sent a letter to George David Banks, who handles international energy issues at the NEC, urging that the U.S. remain in the Paris agreement so “the United States can leverage competitive advantages in natural gas and energy technology.”

title: Sanders turns up the heat on Trump: use defense contracts to save Carrier jobs!
text: Bernie Sanders isn't letting this one go! U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders ramped up the pressure on President-elect Donald Trump on Saturday over his pledge to try to stop an Indiana air conditioner manufacturer from shipping 1,400 jobs to Mexico. Both Sanders, who challenged Hillary Clinton for the Democratic nomination, and Trump seized on an announcement earlier this year by United Technologies Corp's Carrier division that it would shift production to Mexico as proof of how trade deals hurt U.S. workers. Sanders on Saturday warned “it is not good enough to save some of these jobs” and said Trump should use as leverage United Technologies' defense contracts, Export-Import Bank financing, and tax breaks. “I call on Mr. Trump to make it clear to the CEO of United Technologies that if his firm wants to receive another defense contract from the taxpayers of this country, it must not move these plants to Mexico,” the senator from Vermont said in a statement. Carrier's response? A representative declined to comment on Sanders' statement. Trump, who takes office on Jan. 20, said on Thursday that he was “working hard, even on Thanksgiving” to get the plant to stay and said he was “making progress” on the issue. Carrier Corp. confirmed it had “discussions with the incoming administration.” But neither side has provided details. Trump had threatened to slap taxes on the company's air conditioners made in Mexico and shipped back to the United States. A spokesman was not immediately available for comment on Sanders' statement on Saturday. And Sanders is going further: he said he would soon introduce legislation that would bar companies that outsource from receiving federal contracts, grants and loans, and force companies that outsource jobs to pay a penalty tax and pay back tax breaks.

title: Man shouts racial slur and fires at campaign headquarters of Black sheriff candidate
text: On Monday, as a crowd of supporters gathered inside the campaign headquarters of Zena Stephens, an African-American woman running for Sheriff of Jefferson County, Texas, a man opened fire on the building. Witnesses said a white man shouted a profanity and a racial slur against Black people before opening fire from the passenger side of a white jeep. No one was injured in the attack, but the glass doors leading into Stephens' campaign headquarters were shattered. Stephens said the weapon appeared to be either a BB gun or an air rifle. A person from Stephens' campaign headquarters followed the vehicle, helping police locate and apprehend the suspects. Five people have been detained in connection with the incident. Anytime you try to hurt somebody it's just ignorance." The incident is a clear case of voter intimidation, and whoever fired the shot should be punished to the fullest extent of the law. The words the shooter used, reported as either of two phrases containing the same racial slur, leave no doubt that this was a racially motivated hate crime. title: Shots fired at campaign office of Texas sheriff candidate Zena Stephens
text: A man fired at the campaign headquarters of Zena Stephens, an African-American woman running for Sheriff of Jefferson County, Texas, on Monday as a crowd of supporters gathered inside. Witnesses said a white man shouted a profanity and a racial slur against Black people before firing from the passenger side of a white jeep. No one was injured. The glass doors leading into the headquarters were shattered. Stephens said the weapon appeared to be a BB gun or an air rifle. A person from the campaign followed the vehicle and helped police locate and apprehend the suspects. Five people were detained in connection with the incident. Stephens described the attack as an example of ignorance. "Whether we're getting ready for an election or not," the candidate said, "it's just an example of ignorance. Anytime you try to hurt somebody it's just ignorance." The incident was a clear case of voter intimidation, and whoever fired the shot should be punished to the fullest extent of the law. The words the shooter used, reported as either of two phrases containing the same racial slur, left no doubt that it was a racially motivated hate crime. Ahead of Super Tuesday, white supremacists began placing robocalls supporting Donald Trump.

title: Florida ends contract with Youth Services International but keeps for-profit juvenile prisons
text: The Florida Department of Juvenile Justice has decided to end its relationship with the for-profit prison company Youth Services International, whose name is misleading. For years the company has been involved in controversies including covering up sexual abuse of youths by staff, falsifying records and starving inmates, among many other allegations made over the past few years. The company agreed to pay the state of Florida $2 million to have a lawsuit dismissed, and it continues to deny that the lawsuit has any merit. Florida's entire juvenile prison system is privatized, which exposes it to abuse and corruption as the companies holding government contracts seek to maximize profits. Despite the widespread problems with Youth Services International, the state of Florida is only accepting new applications from other for-profit prison companies. "These private prisons interfere with the administration of justice. And they're driving inmate populations skyward by corrupting the political process," Senator Bernie Sanders wrote in a Huffington Post article last year. "No one, in my view, should be allowed to profit from putting more people behind bars whether they're inmates in jail or immigrants held in detention centers. In fact, I believe that private prisons shouldn't be allowed to exist at all, which is why I've introduced legislation to eliminate them." Sanders went on to explain how the for-profit prison system facilitates prisoner abuse, harms minorities, victimizes immigrants, and influences prison policy and immigration policy while corrupting politicians to favor the interests of the for-profit prison industrial complex.

title: Proposal calls on Obama to pardon Hillary Clinton
text: President Obama could heal a divided nation by pardoning Hillary Clinton. If a pardon was appropriate for Richard Nixon, it is appropriate for Clinton. The difference is that Nixon was guilty of the crimes alleged against him, whereas the former Secretary of State, who was thoroughly investigated and cleared of any criminal wrongdoing twice, continues to be criticized and pursued by the right-wing establishment and by political figures with decades-old grudges. They view the investigations of Clinton as an opportunity for revenge against the woman who should be the first female President of the United States, as shown by her winning the national popular vote, though not the electoral college, which is outdated. As originally proposed by former presidential candidate Rev. Jesse Jackson, the nation should call on President Barack Obama to issue a blanket pardon to Clinton, who has been exonerated twice, in order to end the prolonged attacks on the former New York senator's character. In the 21st century, it is difficult to accept that U.S. citizens would seek to stop an accomplished and admired public servant from holding the highest office in the nation because she is a woman. Although the theory is troubling, there is strong evidence to support it, particularly when considering examples from other nations that have had female leaders: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi (1966-77; 1980 to Oct. 31, 1984, when she was assassinated) and British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher (1979-90). Thatcher was the longest-serving British prime minister of the 20th century and the first woman to hold the office.

title: Bloodshed after U.N. vote: Israeli troops kill two Palestinians as Jerusalem fury explodes
text: The anger is boiling over! Israeli troops shot dead at least two Palestinians and wounded about 60 with live fire on Friday, the Health Ministry in Gaza said, as protests intensified against Washington's recognition of Jerusalem as Israel's capital. A U.N. General Assembly resolution passed on Thursday, rejecting U.S. President Donald Trump's Dec. 6 Jerusalem declaration, did little to calm Palestinian fury over his reversal of decades-old U.S. policy on the contested holy city. Instead, thousands of Palestinian protesters, many of them hurling rocks, confronted Israeli security forces along the Gaza border fence, in all seven cities of the occupied West Bank and in East Jerusalem. In Bethlehem, the traditional birthplace of Jesus, smoke from burning tires billowed in the street, just two days before Christmas celebrations. Israeli gunfire killed two Palestinians in a confrontation in the southern Gaza Strip, a spokesman for the Palestinian Health Ministry said, putting the number of wounded at 120, half of them shot with live ammunition and the rest struck by rubber bullets or hit by tear gas canisters. The Israeli military said some 2,000 Palestinians had faced off against the troops at the Gaza border fence. It said the crowd threw stones and rolled burning tires at soldiers, who responded with riot dispersal measures and fired live rounds selectively towards "main instigators". Protesters chanted "Trump is a coward. Trump is a fool". Among the wounded? A man dressed as Santa Claus! Palestinian health officials said at least one Palestinian suffered a live bullet wound in the West Bank and some 30 protesters were hit by rubber bullets. The military, putting the number of demonstrators at about 1,700 and the injured at six, said troops faced firebombs, rocks and burning tires. The protests died down only after sunset.
